ProjectWeave request for the selected Task (data):
{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOLEgSIs8AAAABZguWuw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bm7fazhDHyYU", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bm7fa", "number": 45, "title": "Establish Quest VR controller tracking and dragging in pinned official applications", "body": "## Problem

Quest VR lacks recorded compatibility evidence for applications that continuously consume controller rays/grips and manipulate selected objects. Existing Firefox evidence covers basic VR and ballshooter; historical Chromium Samples coverage does not include Input Tracking. Neither browser has a recorded dragging outcome.

Test implementation and earlier passing scenarios do not establish these application behaviors.

## Expected outcome

Provide working controller tracking, rendering and object dragging in four scenarios: the pinned WebXR Input Tracking Sample and official Three.js dragging example, each on desktop Chromium and Firefox using the actual extension. Fix production defects necessary for those scenarios and record reproducible execution evidence.

## Context

Start from `dev`, evaluated at `7af3ae3aff6c8bd18167155fa5c21add2bd10d14`. All 44 existing Issues/PRs are closed; no dedicated tracking/dragging task exists. This extends the bounded Firefox prerequisite in #37/#38. Earlier administrative closure of #11 retained unfinished compatibility requirements.

Required scenarios use `Meta Quest 3`, `immersive-vr`, stereo enabled and DOM Overlay Preview disabled:

| Application | Pinned revision | Browsers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [input-tracking.html](https://github.com/immersive-web/webxr-samples/blob/fb41c3416496974672e2c766a41c6febcba2d07e/input-tracking.html) | Samples `fb41c3416496974672e2c766a41c6febcba2d07e` | Chromium, Firefox |
| [webxr_xr_dragging.html](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/9b4a2ac29c63ccb43fd51c5661f2f873ac2c39b8/examples/webxr_xr_dragging.html) | Three.js r186 `9b4a2ac29c63ccb43fd51c5661f2f873ac2c39b8` | Chromium, Firefox |

Input Tracking starts an inline session, requests immersive `local-floor`, and renders rays, two-metre cursors and grip models. It deliberately has no button interaction. Dragging uses XRButton, which selects VR under the selected Quest VR policy and requests optional `local-floor`, `bounded-floor`, `layers` and `depth-sensing`; its unchanged depth preferences are `gpu-optimized` and an empty format list. Record actual negotiation; current VR policy omits depth sensing. Neither application requires a new controller feature descriptor.

Follow the pinned [Device CRD, 9 June 2026](https://www.w3.org/TR/2026/CRD-webxr-20260609/) for source identity, relative poses, input events and ownership. Successful trigger completion delivers `selectstart`, then `select` and `selectend`. Inactive frames and foreign-session spaces produce `InvalidStateError`. The [Layers WD, 11 August 2026](https://www.w3.org/TR/2026/WD-webxrlayers-1-20260811/#initialization) permits projection layers independently of requesting `layers`.

Relevant architecture: `src/app/panel.ts` controls feed extension routing, `EmulatedXRDevice.ts` and `device-adapter.ts`; `api/runtime.ts` owns input wrappers, poses, events and frames; base/projection rendering uses `api/layers.ts` and allocation helpers. Reuse `tests/firefox-driver.ts`, `firefox-upstream.ts`, observation helpers and Chromium CDP/panel helpers. The current Chromium Samples runner uses hosted pages and lacks these scenarios. The extension's Three.js dependency is 0.186.1; do not assume it is identical to the pinned application libraries.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Provide a documented focused command or selector for exactly these four scenarios, reusing existing tooling. Use fresh browser profiles, the real unpacked/generated extension and genuine inspected-tab panel. Record browser/build and driver versions; clean up owned processes, profiles and temporary installation on success and failure.
- [ ] Execute unchanged pinned application/library sources with normal API exposure and unchanged feature requests. Supply activation through application entry controls. Drive virtual poses/buttons through actual panel handlers; observation must preserve receivers, arguments, results and exceptions. Do not fabricate page XR events or directly substitute input/application state.
- [ ] Each scenario renders at least 30 immersive callbacks with positive-sized left/right views and identifiable application pixels in the presented output. Record the Sample's base-layer path and Three.js's normally selected projection path. Initialization, background pixels or callback counts alone are insufficient.
- [ ] In Input Tracking, independently translate and rotate both handed controllers and move the viewer. Demonstrate corresponding application-consumed ray, cursor and grip transforms, plus visible output changes. Identify units and tolerances. Do not require button effects from this Sample.
- [ ] In dragging, aim at an existing generated object, press select, move/rotate the controller and release. Record the same object's attachment, changed world transform while held, return to its original group and stable released placement after further controller movement. Repeat with the other handed source. Observe actual application behavior without repositioning objects or replacing its selection logic.
- [ ] Check stable source/ray/grip/profile identities while moving, correct event-source identity and usable event-frame poses during dragging. Adapt the assertions in pinned WPT `xrInputSource_sameObject.https.html` and `xrFrame_lifetime.https.html`, documenting replacement of native fake-device setup. Check inactive-frame and foreign-session-space errors in the focused fixture; distinguish adapted assertions from full WPT execution.
- [ ] End through each application's control, verify one end event and no further callbacks for that ended immersive session, then restart and repeat meaningful tracking/dragging without stale pressed input. Preserve the Sample's separate inline session and its resumption after immersive exit, including #43/#44's visibility correction. Demonstrate that ended-session input/resources do not drive the restarted presentation.
- [ ] Using locked dependencies, run `npm run build:firefox` (including typecheck/build), the focused Chromium and Firefox commands, and `git diff --check`. Fix defects exposed within this scope. Record exact commands, tested source/bundle hashes, served upstream hashes, resolved external dependency/asset provenance, numerical observations, screenshots, failures, skips and unperformed checks. Update reproduction documentation and inventory. Existing reports remain historical evidence; preserve every other actionable goal dimension.

The Coordinator owns implementation, execution, normal PR review and merge. This task adds no independent AI re-review or generic application-suite rerun.

Correct mistaken AI-authored requirements using primary evidence without human approval or independent AI re-review. Retain the original assumption, correction, pinned source and rationale in this Issue/PR. Preserve the goal and meaningful acceptance; unfinished code or failures are not grounds to weaken them.

## Optional validation

Additional browser versions or application/profile combinations. They do not block this four-scenario scope.

## Required post-merge verification

None required.

## Specification reconciliation

This task was authored by AI under the agreed WebXR API compatibility goal for
Quest 3 VR/MR and Android AR. Correct erroneous technical assumptions or acceptance
criteria when primary specifications or measured evidence establish the correction.
Update this Issue and record the original
assumption, corrected requirement, primary reference and rationale in the PR.
These technical corrections require neither human approval nor an independent AI
re-review. Preserve the agreed goal and relevant pre-merge acceptance; do not weaken
requirements merely to accommodate incomplete implementation or failing tests.
